planting.note: Plant divisions after last frost in the warmest, most wind-sheltered microclimate available (south wall or courtyard), in moist, fertile soil in full sun; mulch heavily going into winter, since the pseudostem is often killed back some winters but the rhizome resprouts.

directions: The classic short, fruiting Cavendish selection long grown as a dooryard banana across the Gulf South. In zone 9a, grow it as a ratoon crop: expect the pseudostem to die back some winters, but a heavily mulched rhizome resprouts and can bloom and fruit within 9 to 15 months of resprouting given a long enough frost-free run. Thin excess pups to concentrate energy into the fruiting stem.
sources: UF/IFAS Extension - Bananas in the Florida Garden

planting.note: Grow in an 8-20 gallon container outdoors through the warm season, then move to a bright garage, sunroom, or greenhouse before first frost in marginal zones.

directions: An extreme-dwarf Cavendish selection bred for pot culture, distinct from standard Dwarf Cavendish, giving Gulf gardeners without a frost-free microclimate a practical way to fruit a banana: grow in a container outdoors through summer and overwinter it under cover. Fruit set is inconsistent on overwintered plants since each pseudostem needs a long unbroken warm run to bloom and mature a bunch, but the compact size makes multi-year container culture realistic in a way standard-size cultivars aren't.

planting.note: Transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after last frost; plant several seedlings and cull male plants after flowering, keeping about one male per ten females, since this strain is typically dioecious.

directions: A Mexican-type papaya strain explicitly recommended over Hawaiian Solo-type papayas for Gulf Coast gardens because it is more cold-tolerant and heat and humidity adapted. In marginal zone 8b to 9a plantings, cut the stem to near ground level just before a hard freeze and insulate the crown with deep mulch; the plant resprouts from the base the following spring and fruits from late summer through frost in its second season.
sources: Mobile County Alabama Master Gardeners - Growing Papayas on the Gulf Coast
California Rare Fruit Growers Papaya fact sheet

planting.note: Plant container vines after last frost on a sturdy trellis in full sun with excellent drainage; expect top growth to die back in a hard frost with reliable spring resprouting from the root.

directions: A Passiflora cincinnata by P. incarnata hybrid in the lineage of the already-present Incense, bred for improved flowering and fruit set over its parent. In zone 8-9 Gulf gardens it behaves like maypop, with top growth killed by hard frost but the crown resprouting vigorously from the root each spring. Because it is a hybrid between a tropical and a temperate species, flower and fruit production benefits from the long hot Gulf Coast summer.
sources: growingfruit.org - Hardy Edible Passiflora Hybrids Pedigrees

planting.note: Plant container vines after last frost on a sturdy trellis in full sun with excellent drainage; fruiting improves in year two and beyond as the root system establishes.

directions: A tetraploid seedling selection from the already-present Incense, itself a Passiflora cincinnata by P. incarnata hybrid, chosen for larger flowers and notably better fruit set than its parent. Like other incarnata-derived hybrids, expect full top-kill in a zone 8b to 9a winter with reliable spring resprouting from the root. Give it the same trellis-and-full-sun treatment as maypop.
sources: growingfruit.org - Hardy Edible Passiflora Hybrids Pedigrees
